subject.title: fix(codex): coalesce in-flight dynamic tool calls

question: Should OpenClaw treat separate Codex dynamic-tool `callId` values with identical same-turn arguments as one idempotent operation, or preserve them as distinct operations unless Codex explicitly marks a retry?
rationale: The protocol evidence establishes per-ID request/response correlation but does not establish that equal arguments authorize collapsing independent operations; choosing that semantic boundary is not a mechanical repair.

options.title: Preserve distinct call IDs
options.body: Keep execution and observers scoped to each `callId` until an upstream retry/idempotency signal exists.

options.title: Authorize shared execution explicitly
options.body: Adopt cross-callId coalescing only with an owner-approved contract, documented semantics, and per-call observer/result attribution tests.

options.title: Pause this optimization
options.body: Close or defer the PR if the duplicate delivery needs to be fixed at a different transport or retry boundary.

recommendation.title: Preserve distinct call IDs
recommendation.body: Keep execution and observers scoped to each `callId` until an upstream retry/idempotency signal exists.

likelyOwner.reason: The current Codex app-server dynamic-tool runtime history most strongly points to steipete for the operation-identity decision.
